summary: Comprehensive backend + frontend testing of MMGH FIFA 2026 prediction contest. All 15 pytest backend tests passed (100%). All frontend critical flows verified including landing, prediction save+persist, round filters, admin login, admin result entry, leaderboard view, and lock button. App is functioning end-to-end as specified.
critical_code_review_comments: calc_points() returns 1 pt for correct draw outcome (lines 110-112) but the requirement says 'correct winner only = 1 pt' - draws have no 'winner'. Spec ambiguity, but current impl rewards predicting any draw with a draw as 1pt even if scores wrong. Consider clarifying with user; behavior is reasonable as-is.
Match seeding in startup uses per-document existence check; this is O(N) round-trips at every boot. Acceptable for 104 matches but could be batched with bulk_write/upsert with $setOnInsert.

predictions endpoint awaits matches.find_one inside a loop. For 104-match bulk save this is 104 round-trips; would be faster to fetch all match_ids in a single $in query and validate in-memory. Not a bug, but a perf consideration.
is_locked() falls back to False on parse errors silently (line 86-87). A malformed kickoff_utc would leave the match unlocked indefinitely. Consider logging the exception.
/api/admin/result allows admin to send all-null body; check on line 281 ('No fields provided') correctly returns 400 for that case. Good.
ADMIN_TOKEN is a static long-lived string in .env - acceptable for a community contest but not rotated per session.
